question.prompt: How many different isosceles triangles have integer side lengths and perimeter \(23?\)

solutions.explanation:
Let the two equal sides have positive integer length \(a\), and let the third side have length \(b\). The perimeter condition gives
\[
b=23-2a.
\]
Since \(b\) must be a positive integer, \(a\le11\).

The two equal sides must together be longer than the third side, so
\[
2a>23-2a,
\qquad 4a>23.
\]
Thus the integer \(a\) must be at least \(6\). The other two triangle inequalities hold automatically because \(a+b>a\) whenever \(b>0\).

Consequently, every integer \(a\) from \(6\) through \(11\) works. The corresponding third sides are \(11,9,7,5,3,1\), respectively. These exhaust the possibilities. Since \(23\) is not divisible by \(3\), none is equilateral, so each triangle has a unique repeated side length and is counted once. There are
\[
11-6+1=\boxed{6}
\]
triangles, choice C.
solutions.title: Bound the equal side length
